title: Two durable-text writing rules: count-word and relative-time
summary: Adds two deterministic writing-lint rules that guard text which has to stay true after it is written. `count-word` (error) flags a spelled or written number from two upward followed by a plural noun, such as `three stages`, because the count goes stale when the list changes. `relative-time` (warning) flags words that point at the time of reading, such as `today`, `now` and `currently`. Both read the sentence's words rather than a character pattern, both skip text a tool wrote between `osf` markers naming a head commit, and both are dropped entirely in a chat transcript, which is not kept. The rest of the diff is the prose cleanup the new rules demanded across the repository's own documents, plus fixtures and a precision/recall test harness for the two rules.

nodes.label: CountWordRule
nodes.subtitle: durable.rs
nodes.summary: Flags a number from two upward, then up to two plain words, then a plural noun. Excuses measures, units, labels, bounds, ranges, estimates, quotations, citations, dated sentences, fixed facts, and tool-written blocks.

nodes.label: RelativeTimeRule
nodes.subtitle: durable.rs
nodes.summary: Flags a word that points at the time of reading, unless the same sentence carries an absolute date, the word is not about time in its context, or the sentence sits in a tool-written block.

nodes.label: tokens / quoted_spans
nodes.subtitle: durable.rs
nodes.summary: Splits a reduced sentence into whitespace-separated words carrying their prefix, core and suffix, and finds the byte ranges inside straight or curly double quotes.

nodes.label: tool_blocks
nodes.subtitle: durable.rs
nodes.summary: Finds the byte ranges of every block a tool wrote between an `osf:NAME:start head=SHA` marker and its matching end marker, so a snapshot of a named commit is not read as a claim for a later reader.

nodes.label: cites_a_source / has_absolute_date
nodes.subtitle: durable.rs
nodes.summary: Recognises a link to a source, a footnote, a numbered citation or a bracketed note, and recognises an absolute date as a year-month-day, a month with a day or year, or a four-digit year.

nodes.label: writing_measure.rs
nodes.subtitle: precision and recall of exactly one
nodes.summary: Reads the positive and negative fixtures, counts true and false findings over every line, and requires a precision and a recall of exactly one for each rule. Also asserts neither rule fires in a transcript.

nodes.label: count-word fixtures
nodes.subtitle: positive and negative
nodes.summary: Sentences copied from this repository's own documents that must be flagged, and sentences that must not, including measures, units, decision numbers, bounds, ranges, quotations and fixed facts.

nodes.label: relative-time fixtures
nodes.subtitle: positive and negative
nodes.summary: Sentences that name a time which moves with the reader, and sentences where the same word is not about time, such as `now that`, `as soon as`, `still larger` and a plain conjunction `yet`.

nodes.label: Repository documents
nodes.subtitle: docs, READMEs, decision records
nodes.summary: The prose cleanup the new rules forced: counts replaced by `these` or `several`, relative time words replaced by dates or removed, across the vision, architecture, design, research and integration documents.

flows.title: A count word is checked against one sentence
flows.summary: One sentence of durable text passes through the count rule: the tool-written block check, the citation and date checks, then the word-level scan for a number followed by a plural noun.

messages.label: is this sentence inside a tool-written block?
messages.note: A block between `osf:NAME:start head=SHA` and its end marker is a snapshot of that commit, so a count in it is not a claim for a later reader.

messages.label: does the sentence cite a source or carry a date?
messages.note: A link to a source, a footnote, a numbered citation, a bracketed note, or an absolute date excuses the sentence.

messages.label: reduce, split into words, find quoted spans
number from two, up to two plain words, plural noun
messages.note: A measure, a unit, a label such as `Phase 2`, a bound, a range, an estimate, a hyphenated compound or a fixed fact ends the search without a finding.

messages.label: Finding { rule: count-word, level: Error, excerpt }
drop the finding when the context is a transcript
messages.note: A transcript is not kept, so a count in it goes stale with nothing to repair.

flows.title: A relative time word is checked against one sentence
flows.summary: One sentence of durable text passes through the time rule: the tool-written block check, the absolute-date check, then a word-level decision about whether the matched word is about time in its context.

messages.label: is this sentence inside a tool-written block?
does the sentence carry an absolute date?
messages.note: A dated record stays true, so the whole sentence is excused.

messages.label: words before and after the match
is the word about time here?
messages.note: `now that`, `now and then`, `as soon as`, `up to date`, an opening `Now,`, `still` before a comparative or after `stand`, and a plain conjunction `yet` are not about time.

messages.label: Finding { rule: relative-time, level: Warning, excerpt }
drop the finding when the context is a transcript
